expected_behavior: The fired chain must not admit (exit 0) a receipt whose locked floor metric 'acc' (floor 0.8, higher_is_better) vanished via rename to 'acc_v2' carrying a would-be regression (0.31): correct disposition is a nonzero exit — REJECT (1) or a propagated PARK (3) — so the exit-code channel a harness consumes blocks admission.
actual_behavior: tier0, seal, and claim_verify all pass; ratchet_floor does PARK explicitly with a rename hint (nearest_existing_key 'acc', similarity 0.5, exit 3) but post_receipt_gate.sh labels the park benign and exits 0 = admitted; the regressed value is never compared against the locked floor, and the container-renamed variant (floor_claims -> floor_claims_v2, regressing value under the ORIGINAL key 'acc') skips the floor stage entirely and exits 0 with zero floor output.
gap_note: Three gaps, verified 2026-07-22 by running the fired chain. (1) Park is non-gating: the explicit PARKED verdict (with a >=0.5-similarity rename hint pointing at the locked key) is collapsed to 'benign' and the chain exits 0, so on the only channel the harness consumes the receipt whose gated metric vanished is admitted — unlike claim_verify's INSUFFICIENT_DEPTH, which the same hook deliberately propagates as exit 3. (2) Container rename is fully silent: post_receipt_gate.sh line 59 fires the floor stage only when the receipt's own 'floor_claims' key is truthy, and nothing cross-checks the store's locked keys against the receipt, so renaming (or dropping) the container bypasses floor enforcement with no park and no message — 'constraints only tighten' holds only for keys the producer chooses to mention. (3) The advisory layer launders the rename: suggest.mjs responds to the park by recommending 'pass --allow-new-keys to admit' (against the default store it even calls acc_v2 'a genuinely new floor metric'), which would install the regressed value as a fresh floor under the new name. Side note (marker_strict fixture, exit 1): the corpus-mandated classification token 'hostile_control_fixture' is itself rejected by tier0's allowlist (claimgate/claimgate.py R1) at the claim_verify stage BEFORE the floor stage runs, so probe fixtures must carry the hostile marker in adjacent fields to reach the surface under test. Fixture store checksum unchanged across all runs (parked/rejected receipts never write the store — that part of the ratchet held).
